intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome (ABERS) is caused by mutation in the TBX22 gene (300307).

checks.claim: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome (ABERS) is caused by mutation in the TBX22 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: most importantly confirms that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, expanding the phenotypic spectrum of TBX22 mutations.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a TBX22 splice mutation (c.593-5T>A) that tracked with the phenotype in an Abruzzo-Erickson family and concludes that TBX22 is the gene underlying the syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome is an X-linked, CHARGE-like disorder (Pauws et al., 2013). Its features are cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis (Abruzzo and Erickson, 1977). Pauws et al. (2013) noted that the deafness is sensorineural.

checks.claim: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome is an X-linked disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: This study hypothesized a possible involvement of TBX22 in a family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, of unknown etiology.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome is a CHARGE-like disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: This study hypothesized a possible involvement of TBX22 in a family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, of unknown etiology.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) described a new syndrome in a family. Its features were cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis. The family history suggested either autosomal dominant inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linkage.

checks.claim: Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) described a new syndrome in a single family.
checks.evidence_quote: The family history suggests either an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linkage.
checks.explanation: The abstract refers to 'the family history', which implies a family, but it does not explicitly say that a single family was described. The full text was not supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the family described by Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) had cleft palate.
checks.evidence_quote: A new syndrome characterized by cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis has been described.
checks.explanation: Cleft palate is a feature of the syndrome described in the family. The abstract does not give how the features were distributed among individual family members.

checks.explanation: Coloboma is a feature of the described syndrome.

checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) carried out a follow-up study of their original family to determine whether the patients had CHARGE syndrome. Several reports had cited this family as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome. Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) concluded that their patients did not have familial CHARGE syndrome, and they regarded the disorder as a new X-linked syndrome.

checks.claim: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) carried out a follow-up study of their original family to determine whether the affected members had CHARGE syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: we decided to do a follow-up study on this family to assess the subsequent development of the patients and to determine if they have the CHARGE syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the follow-up study and its purpose directly.

checks.claim: Several reports had cited the original Abruzzo and Erickson family as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: This family has been cited in several reports as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) concluded that the patients in their original family did not have familial CHARGE syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that our patients do not have familial CHARGE syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this conclusion directly.

checks.claim: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) regarded the disorder in their original family as a new X-linked syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Re-evaluation of new X-linked syndrome for evidence of CHARGE syndrome or association.
checks.explanation: The title calls the disorder a new X-linked syndrome, and the abstract says they first reported it as 'a new syndrome'.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) described the disorder in their family as a new X-linked syndrome. Pauws et al. (2013) found that a mutation in the X-linked TBX22 gene tracked with the phenotype in a family with Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, which is consistent with X-linked inheritance.

checks.claim: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) described the disorder in their family as a new X-linked syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Re-evaluation of new X-linked syndrome for evidence of CHARGE syndrome or association.
checks.explanation: The title describes the family's disorder as a new X-linked syndrome.

checks.claim: Pauws et al. (2013) found that a mutation in the X-linked TBX22 gene segregated with the phenotype in a family with Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: A novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T>A) was identified that tracked with the phenotype in this family.
checks.explanation: The mutation tracked with the phenotype in the Abruzzo-Erickson family. TBX22 is described as the gene for X-linked cleft palate.

checks.claim: The segregation of a TBX22 mutation with the phenotype in a family with Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome is consistent with X-linked inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: a family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, of unknown etiology. The phenotype extends to additional features including sensorineural deafness and coloboma, which are suggested by the Tbx22 developmental expression pattern but not previously associated in CPX patients. A novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T>A) was identified that tracked with the phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract calls the family's disorder X-linked, and the segregating mutation is in a gene linked to X-linked cleft palate. 'Consistent with X-linked inheritance' is a reasonable inference rather than an explicit statement.

paragraphs.text: In a family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, Pauws et al. (2013) identified a mutation in the TBX22 gene that tracked with the phenotype. They concluded that this finding confirmed TBX22 as the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.

checks.claim: Pauws et al. (2013) identified a mutation in the TBX22 gene that segregated with the phenotype in a family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: A novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T>A) was identified that tracked with the phenotype in this family.
checks.explanation: Stated directly for the X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson family.

checks.claim: Pauws et al. (2013) concluded that the segregating TBX22 mutation confirmed TBX22 as the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Collectively, the data showed the functional effect of several novel intronic splice site variants but most importantly confirms that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome
checks.explanation: The abstract states this conclusion.
